title: Jude and the Signal
premise: Isandro Eastwick, a xenolinguist turned cargo hauler haunted by dreams in a language no human speaks, discovers her name on the manifest of the Meridian, a ship that was destroyed twenty years ago — the same ship her mother died aboard. The manifest is a coded message left by her mother, a translator who uncovered proof that the war between the orbital coalitions began on a fabricated signal, and who hid the evidence inside an alien linguistic cipher only Isandro can read. Pursued by both warring factions, Isandro must decode and deliver the message to a neutral arbiter station before the Meridian's derelict reactor — still counting down after two decades — detonates and destroys the proof forever. She succeeds at terrible cost: the truth ends the war, but she loses the ship, her partner-in-flight Jude, and the version of herself that could still dream in human words.
about_author: Tamsin Reyes is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write fiction about the people history forgets to record. She lives aboard a converted ferry with her partner and an unreasonable number of dictionaries.

chapters.title: Dead Letter Orbit
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Hauling scrap through contested orbits, she receives a salvage ping for the Meridian — a ship lost twenty years ago with her mother aboard. The manifest lists Isandro Eastwick as crew. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath professional detachment.

chapters.title: The Name That Shouldn't Fit
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She verifies the manifest against guild records; the signature is her mother's hand, dated three days after the Meridian's destruction. Her port contact warns her to walk away. Beat: denial hardening into compulsion.

chapters.title: Jude
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude Okonkwo, Isandro's engineer and quiet partner, notices Isandro pulling old flight logs and confronts her gently. They argue about debts owed to the dead versus the living. Beat: love expressed as friction.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Vessic
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A flashback chapter: young Isandro learning alien languages from her mother, and the first night she dreamed in Vessic instead of English. Establishes her gift as inheritance and burden. Beat: tender melancholy.

chapters.title: Charter of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She charters a jump to the Meridian's last known coordinates under a false cargo declaration. The broker is nervous; someone else has asked about the same wreck this month. Beat: the trap beginning to close.

chapters.title: What the Reactor Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Approaching the derelict, Jude reads its telemetry: the reactor never shut down, it's been counting down for twenty years on some corrupted cycle. Beat: awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Boarding the Meridian
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. They board the cold hulk. Personal effects float in zero-g; Isandro finds her own childhood drawing taped to a cabin wall. Beat: grief arriving like pressure change.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Walls
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the translation bay she finds her mother's terminal, booted and waiting, displaying a message addressed to her in Vessic. It begins: 'If you are reading this, they let you live long enough.' Beat: vertigo of being expected.

chapters.title: First Decoding
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The message is layered: surface text, then a cipher keyed to Vessic grammar patterns only a native-level dreamer could parse. She decodes the first fragment — coordinates and one word: 'fabricated.' Beat: exhilaration shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Visitors
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. An unmarked cutter docks uninvited. Jude hides Isandro and stalls the boarding party — coalition 'salvage assessors' who scan for data cores. Beat: terror managed through competence.

chapters.title: The Assessor's Smile
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The assessor, Captain Rhee, knows exactly who Isandro is and offers her safe passage home if she surrenders the terminal. Isandro lies for the first time in her life. Beat: the moment duty flips allegiance.

chapters.title: Undocking Under Guns
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A hair-raising departure through debris fields while Rhee's cutter pursues. Jude burns reserve fuel they'll need later. Beat: adrenaline and mutual trust forged under fire.

chapters.title: Fragment Two: The Signal
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Decoded fragment reveals the war's opening attack was triggered by a signal no faction sent — manufactured by a third party profiting from the conflict. Beat: righteous anger replacing fear.

chapters.title: Harbor of Thieves
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. They dock at Ceres Freeport to resupply and find a neutral courier. The station is a maze of informants; Isandro trades a decoded phrase for fuel. Beat: moral compromise in a lawless place.

chapters.title: The Courier Who Refused
chapters.summary: New character POV: Sefa, an aging neutral courier, refuses the job — the last two couriers carrying similar messages died. But she gives Isandro a name: the Arbiter at Station Halcyon. Beat: kindness from a stranger.

chapters.title: Rhee Finds Them
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Coalition marines raid the berth. Jude holds a corridor alone so Isandro can escape with the core. He's captured. Beat: sacrifice without announcement.

chapters.title: Alone With the Language
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Fleeing solo, she decodes fragment three: her mother didn't die in the attack — she was executed for discovering the fabrication, and the countdown on the Meridian is deliberate, a dead-man's switch. Beat: rage and heartbreak braided together.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Rhee interrogates Jude, not cruelly but patiently, offering him Isandro's safety in exchange for the core's location. Jude realizes Rhee isn't coalition — he's working for the fabricators. Beat: quiet defiance.

chapters.title: The Dream That Isn't Hers
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Sleeping rough in Freeport's underlevels, Isandro dreams fully in Vessic for the first time in years — and wakes knowing a word she never learned: her mother's word for 'witness.' Beat: inheritance becoming communion.

chapters.title: Buying a Ship With Lies
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Stranded, she cons a smuggler out of a battered jump tug using forged guild credentials and the decoded fragments as bait. Beat: Isandro becoming someone her mother would recognize.

chapters.title: Rhee's Offer, Broadcast
chapters.summary: Rhee's POV (first antagonist interior). Rhee broadcasts a bounty framing Isandro as a war criminal carrying bioweapon data. He believes his own cover story — almost. Beat: antagonist humanized, threat multiplied.

chapters.title: Jude's Bargain
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude escapes captivity during a transfer, stealing a suit pod, and sends a blind transmission Isandro taught him years ago — a Vessic phrase meaning 'follow my echo.' Beat: hope as technical skill.

chapters.title: Echo
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She intercepts Jude's echo and plots an impossible rendezvous through a debris shoal. Beat: love as navigation.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Shoal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The rescue nearly fails; Jude is hypoxic and half-frozen. In the airlock, neither speaks — the Vessic word for witness passes between them. Beat: reunion stripped of sentiment, all substance.

chapters.title: Fragment Four: The Names
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The final layer lists every person paid to sustain the lie — including judges, admirals, and the Arbiter's own predecessor. Delivering it means trusting an institution already compromised. Beat: despair about justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Halcyon or Nowhere
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Debate: deliver to Halcyon's new Arbiter, or broadcast everything publicly and let chaos decide. Isandro chooses the Arbiter because her mother did. Beat: conviction over cynicism.

chapters.title: The Countdown Accelerates
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Remote telemetry shows the Meridian's reactor cycle shortening — someone triggered a remote purge. They have days, not months, before the proof vaporizes. Beat: clock now audible in every scene.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Gate
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Rhee's cutter traps them at the jump gate. Isandro bluffs with a fake copy of the core, buying escape but confirming their route. Beat: cleverness costing them their head start.

chapters.title: What Isandro Owes
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Quiet interlude: she tells Jude the full story of her mother, and admits she boarded the Meridian hoping to find her alive. Grief finally spoken aloud. Beat: intimacy as aftermath.

chapters.title: Rhee's Doubt
chapters.summary: Rhee's POV. Reviewing Isandro's decoded fragments intercepted at the gate, Rhee finds his own name on the payment list — he was a tool, not a partner. Beat: antagonist's crisis of loyalty.

chapters.title: Approach to Halcyon
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Halcyon station demands surrender of all data on approach — standard protocol that would let the compromised apparatus bury the message. Isandro refuses and requests asylum arbitration instead. Beat: law as obstacle and weapon.

chapters.title: Siege of Patience
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Halcyon stalls while factions lobby behind closed doors. Jude repairs the tug, prepping a desperate option: fly back to the Meridian themselves. Beat: tension of waiting.

chapters.title: Rhee Defects
chapters.summary: Rhee's POV. Rhee arrives at Halcyon not to arrest Isandro but to testify, trading his career for the truth. His testimony unlocks the arbitration. Beat: enemy becoming reluctant ally.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Before the Arbiter, Isandro delivers the message — translating the Vessic layers aloud, ending with her mother's final line: 'I was the witness; let her be the voice.' Beat: climax of purpose.

chapters.title: Verdict and Betrayal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Arbiter rules to publish — but a saboteur triggers the Meridian's reactor remotely, forcing immediate evacuation of the evidence site and threatening to destroy the physical originals. Beat: victory poisoned.

chapters.title: Back to the Meridian
chapters.summary: Isandro and Jude's POV. Against orders, they jump to the Meridian to retrieve the physical archive before detonation — a ten-minute window inside a dying ship. Beat: full-circle courage.

chapters.title: Ten Minutes
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Inside the burning hulk of her childhood, Isandro reaches the translation bay as the reactor breaches. Jude drags her out; the archive case survives; part of her doesn't want to leave. Beat: letting go of the dead.

chapters.title: Detonation
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The Meridian explodes as their tug clears the blast radius. The physical proof is secured; the ship that held Isandro's whole inheritance is gone. Beat: catharsis through loss.

chapters.title: The War Ends Quietly
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Across the system, ceasefires take hold as the fabrication goes public; Rhee testifies before tribunals; Sefa the courier carries the news free of charge. Beat: justice arriving without trumpets.

chapters.title: Dreaming Again
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Months later, Isandro and Jude haul honest cargo. One night she dreams in English for the first time in twenty years — and in the dream, her mother says goodbye. Final beat: peace earned, inheritance transformed into choice.
